swap_risks: CRITICAL SUPPLY VOLTAGE RATING: LMV358IDR is limited to 5.5 V max (5.5 V abs max, p.5) whereas NE5532DR supports up to 30 V (36 V abs max, p.3). Installing a 5.5 V CMOS part on a 12 V–24 V rail causes instant breakdown.

HIGH HEADROOM / CLIPPING RISK: Rail-to-rail capability differs (LMV358IDR: IN=Non-RR, OUT=RR vs NE5532DR: IN=Non-RR, OUT=Non-RR); verify input common-mode range (Vicm) and output voltage swing against ADC full-scale range.

CAUTION BANDWIDTH & PHASE MARGIN: GBWP differs by 12x (LMV358IDR: 1 MHz p.7 vs NE5532DR: 12 MHz p.4); higher-bandwidth replacements can oscillate with capacitive loads or stray feedback capacitance without an isolation resistor.
CAUTION SLEW RATE DIFFERENCE: Slew rate differs by 5x (LMV358IDR: 1 V/µs p.7 vs NE5532DR: 5 V/µs p.4); check full-power bandwidth SR / (2π·Vpeak).

HIGH INPUT BIAS CURRENT SHIFT: Typical Ib differs by 13x (LMV358IDR: 15000 pA p.7 vs NE5532DR: 200000 pA p.4); high-impedance sensor dividers (>100 kΩ) suffer severe Ib·R DC offset error when swapping from CMOS/JFET to bipolar inputs.

CAUTION QUIESCENT CURRENT SHIFT: Supply current per channel differs by 28.6x (LMV358IDR: 105 µA/ch p.7 vs NE5532DR: 3000 µA/ch p.4); verify battery budget and total power dissipation across all channels.
HIGH ABSOLUTE-MAX SURGE MARGIN: LMV358IDR has a lower Vs,abs,max rating (5.5 V, p.5) than NE5532DR (36 V, p.3); verify hot-plug, inductive kickback, and TVS clamp peaks stay safely below 5.5 V.
HIGH THERMAL MARGIN: Package θJA is 114% higher on LMV358IDR (LMV358IDR: 207.9 °C/W p.6 vs NE5532DR: 97 °C/W p.3); re-check Tj = Ta + Pd × θJA against Tj,max.
HIGH MINIMUM SUPPLY FLOOR: NE5532DR requires Vs,min >= 10 V (p.3) vs 2.7 V on the counterpart; confirm low-battery / brown-out operation still clears the higher floor.

HIGH TEMPERATURE GRADE MISMATCH: Rated ambient range differs (LMV358IDR: -40..125 °C Extended Industrial (-40°C to 125°C) vs NE5532DR: 0..70 °C Commercial (0°C to 70°C)); NE5532DR cold limit only 0 °C, NE5532DR hot limit only 70 °C — verify product ambient qualification before swapping.
engineering_verdict: LMV358IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and NE5532DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required alternatives: the PCB land pattern is compatible, but passive retuning or rating derating is mandatory because supply voltage Vs,max drops >=20%; rail-to-rail input/output swing differs; GBWP differs 12x. Signal-chain deltas: GBWP 1 MHz (p.7) vs 12 MHz (p.4), supply ceiling 5.5 V (p.5) vs 30 V (p.3), Vos 7 mV (p.7) vs 4 mV (p.4), Ib 13x gap (15000 vs 200000 pA), voltage noise 39 vs 5 nV/√Hz. Primary bench gotchas to watch: LMV358IDR "5.5 V Absolute Maximum Ceiling — Destructive If Swapped into LM358 High-Voltage Boards" (p.5) and NE5532DR "Internal Back-to-Back Input Clamp Diodes Conduct Above ~0.6 V Differential Input" (p.3). BOM decision: Choose LMV358IDR when high-impedance sensors require pA-class input bias (15000 pA) or ultra-low supply current (105 µA/ch) is prioritized; choose NE5532DR when supply rails exceed 5.5 V (rated up to 30 V) or closed-loop signal bandwidth requires 12 MHz GBWP. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.2) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
